original_question: Describe all chiral polytopes of full rank.
target_in_paper: The paper’s main construction-and-proof problem: exhibit the explicit infinite 4-polytope P_{\{\infty,3,4\}} in Euclidean 3-space and prove that it is combinatorially chiral, thereby giving an infinite chiral 4-polytope of full rank.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the theme of the paper: chiral polytopes and the special full-rank setting.
missing_details: The paper does not aim to classify all chiral polytopes of full rank.
Its scope is one explicit example, not a global description theorem.
The object is an infinite polytope, not an arbitrary finite-or-infinite one.
The ambient space is Euclidean 3-space R^3.
The relevant full-rank case here is a rank-4 polytope realized in dimension 3.
The paper’s named object is the specific 4-polytope P_{\{\infty,3,4\}}.
What must be proved is combinatorial chirality of that explicit construction.
The paper builds on an earlier finite example; it does not reclassify the earlier example or all other full-rank chiral polytopes.
The intended outcome is existence via explicit construction, not a complete taxonomy.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite rank-4 polytope of full rank in Euclidean 3-space—that is, a 4-polytope realized in R^3—with chiral combinatorial symmetry? If so, explicitly construct the polytope P_{\{\infty,3,4\}} and prove that it is combinatorially chiral.
justification: The draft is much broader than the paper. The abstract states that the paper describes an infinite chiral 4-polytope in Euclidean 3-space and that, together with earlier work, this shows the existence of finite and infinite chiral polytopes of full rank. The culmination inside the paper is Theorem 5.1, which proves that the explicitly constructed polytope P_{\{\infty,3,4\}} is combinatorially chiral. So the nearest paper-faithful stand-alone question is an existence/construction question for that specific infinite full-rank 4-polytope in R^3, not a classification of all full-rank chiral polytopes.
